page: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, reaching clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. It includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, as well as SHA-NI and AES cryptographic acceleration.

The instance is characterized by a high memory-to-vCPU allocation, supplying 128.0 GB of RAM, or 16.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, requiring reliance on remote persistent storage volumes for stateful data. In benchmark evaluations, the high CPU clock speed translates into top-tier single-core performance, evidenced by top 10% percentiles in Geekbench single-core tests, single-threaded stress-ng execution, and compression tasks such as gzip and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core compute and PassMark CPU metrics reflect mid-tier throughput typical of an 8-vCPU allocation.

Because the E16-8as_v7 features constrained vCPU counts paired with substantial memory capacity, it offers favorable qualitative cost efficiency for software workloads licensed on a per-core basis that demand large memory footprints. The lack of ephemeral local disks requires architecting storage through external network volumes. The instance is well-suited for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, medium-scale relational databases, real-time analytics, and data pipeline tasks that prioritize memory capacity and single-thread execution speed over wide parallel scaling.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. Virtualized using Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 32 MB of L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets. The instance delivers 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It includes no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight top-tier single-threaded performance in Geekbench and compression tasks, balanced by middle-tier multi-threaded throughput. From an operational efficiency perspective, the constrained core count paired with expansive memory reduces per-core software licensing costs. This server is appropriately deployed for memory-bound workloads such as in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, ETL processing, and relational databases that require high memory capacity without large core counts.
